stem: A scheduled Lambda ingestion job completes successfully but sometimes writes far fewer records than expected. Engineers only receive alerts when the function throws. Which approach best detects silent under-production?

options.label: A
options.body: Emit a custom CloudWatch metric for records written per run and alarm when it falls below a baseline

options.label: B
options.body: Increase Lambda memory so the function is less likely to time out

options.label: C
options.body: Wrap business logic in a broad try/except that returns success after logging

options.label: D
options.body: Set reserved concurrency to 1 for the function

explanation: Successful runs with unexpectedly low volume do not raise errors. A throughput metric with a low-threshold alarm detects silent under-production. Memory, swallowed exceptions, and concurrency limits do not measure output volume.

stem: A team will redeploy the same serverless data pipeline across three accounts using infrastructure as code. Which two statements are accurate?

options.label: A
options.body: Version-controlled templates tie each deployment change to a commit and author

options.label: B
options.body: A declarative template can be applied repeatably across accounts without manual console recreation

options.label: C
options.body: IaC requires creating every resource in the console before automation can manage it

options.label: D
options.body: Templated updates always guarantee zero downtime for every resource type

options.label: E
options.body: Passing template syntax validation removes the need to test deployed behavior

explanation: IaC provides traceability and repeatable multi-account deployment. It does not require console-first creation, does not guarantee zero downtime for all updates, and syntax checks are not a substitute for testing.

stem: An AWS Glue ETL job must connect to a legacy database whose engine is not in Glue’s built-in JDBC list. The vendor provided a JDBC driver JAR. How should the driver be supplied?

options.label: A
options.body: Upload the JAR to Amazon S3 and reference that path in the Glue connection so the job loads it at runtime

options.label: B
options.body: Open a support case asking AWS to install the JAR onto Glue’s managed hosts

options.label: C
options.body: Package the JAR as a Lambda layer and attach it to the Glue job

options.label: D
options.body: Replace JDBC with Amazon Data Firehose because Firehose can speak any database protocol

explanation: Glue supports custom JDBC drivers stored in S3 and referenced by the connection. Glue does not use Lambda layers, and Firehose is not a generic JDBC client.

stem: Pipeline A must catalog new S3 partitions once every hour regardless of activity. Pipeline B must start within seconds whenever a new object lands. Which two trigger choices match these needs?

options.label: A
options.body: Use a time-based schedule (cron) for pipeline A’s crawler/job

options.label: B
options.body: Use S3 Event Notifications or EventBridge object-created rules for pipeline B

options.label: C
options.body: Use only object-created events for pipeline A so it never runs on quiet hours

options.label: D
options.body: Use a fixed hourly schedule for pipeline B to poll for new files

options.label: E
options.body: Require manual console starts for both pipelines

explanation: Fixed schedules guarantee hourly runs. Event-driven object notifications meet near-real-time needs. The reverse choices break each requirement.

stem: A Lambda function is mapped to a Kinesis data stream with default event source mapping settings. What is the default read behavior?

options.label: A
options.body: Lambda polls each shard as a standard iterator consumer sharing shard throughput with other consumers

options.label: B
options.body: Lambda always registers enhanced fan-out with dedicated throughput per shard by default

options.label: C
options.body: Lambda invokes once per individual record and never batches

options.label: D
options.body: The stream must be deleted and recreated as a Lambda-only stream type first

explanation: By default Lambda uses shared throughput polling. Enhanced fan-out is optional. Batching is the normal behavior, and no special stream type is required.

stem: A team wants orchestration with no server patching or capacity planning, supporting long-running branching workflows that coordinate Glue, Lambda, and a manual approval. Which option best fits?

options.label: A
options.body: AWS Step Functions Standard workflows

options.label: B
options.body: Self-managed Airflow on a single EC2 instance

options.label: C
options.body: Only Amazon EventBridge Scheduler cron rules with no state machine

options.label: D
options.body: Amazon EMR cluster steps without an orchestration layer

explanation: Step Functions Standard is fully managed/serverless and supports long-running branching and wait-for-callback/approval patterns. Self-managed Airflow adds ops burden; cron alone lacks rich branching state.

stem: Three AWS accounts each run Amazon MWAA. A DAG in account A should trigger a DAG in account B when upstream datasets are ready, without tightly coupling schedules. Which MWAA capability directly supports this pattern?

options.label: A
options.body: Dataset-driven scheduling / data-aware scheduling across DAG dependencies

options.label: B
options.body: Replacing all DAGs with a single shared cron expression in every account

options.label: C
options.body: Hard-coding EC2 public IPs of each MWAA webserver into DAG files

options.label: D
options.body: Disabling concurrency so only one DAG in the organization can run at a time

explanation: Data-aware / dataset scheduling lets DAGs react to asset readiness rather than only wall-clock schedules, which fits loosely coupled cross-team pipelines.

stem: A Step Functions task uses a callback (.waitForTaskToken) pattern. The external worker crashes and never calls SendTaskSuccess or SendTaskFailure. What prevents an indefinite wait?

options.label: A
options.body: Configure a TimeoutSeconds (or HeartbeatSeconds) on the task state

options.label: B
options.body: Disable logging on the state machine

options.label: C
options.body: Switch the state machine type from Standard to Express only

options.label: D
options.body: Remove IAM permissions for SendTaskFailure so failures cannot be reported

explanation: Task-level timeouts/heartbeats bound how long Step Functions waits for a callback. Express vs Standard is about duration/execution model, not a substitute for timeouts.

stem: CSV files uploaded to an S3 prefix must be converted to Parquet by Lambda only when the object key ends with .csv. Which notification design is correct?

options.label: A
options.body: s3:ObjectCreated:* with a suffix filter of .csv targeting the Lambda ARN

options.label: B
options.body: s3:ObjectTagging:* filtered on a tag value of csv

options.label: C
options.body: s3:* with no suffix filter

options.label: D
options.body: ObjectCreated events that only publish to SNS with no Lambda destination and no subscription

explanation: ObjectCreated with a suffix filter ensures Lambda runs only for .csv uploads. Tagging events and unfiltered wildcards do not meet the requirement cleanly.

stem: Nightly Glue jobs are flexible on finish time and should minimize cost. Which job execution class is most appropriate?

options.label: A
options.body: FLEX

options.label: B
options.body: STANDARD only, because FLEX cannot run Glue ETL

options.label: C
options.body: Spot Instance type field in Glue job properties (as if Glue were EC2 Spot bidding UI)

options.label: D
options.body: Setting GlueVersion alone without changing execution class

explanation: Glue FLEX execution class is designed for non-urgent workloads at lower cost. STANDARD is for time-sensitive jobs.

stem: Which two patterns correctly use Amazon Bedrock in a data engineering pipeline?

options.label: A
options.body: Invoke a Bedrock model from Lambda after a crawler run to generate table descriptions for the Glue Data Catalog

options.label: B
options.body: Call Bedrock from an existing Lambda transform to classify free-text support tickets before writing downstream

options.label: C
options.body: Replace Glue crawlers entirely with Bedrock writing catalog schemas directly as a metastore

options.label: D
options.body: Configure Bedrock as a native Glue Spark worker/DPU executor type

options.label: E
options.body: Use Bedrock as the only way to count rows grouped by date

explanation: Bedrock is an API for generative tasks such as descriptions and classification. It is not a catalog replacement, Spark worker type, or required for simple aggregations.

stem: A team needs serverless Spark ETL with minimal cluster management for daily batch jobs that fit Glue’s feature set. When is AWS Glue generally preferable to Amazon EMR?

options.label: A
options.body: When you want a fully managed, serverless Spark job model without sizing and patching clusters

options.label: B
options.body: When you must run arbitrary long-lived multi-tenant YARN applications with custom bootstrap deep OS tuning

options.label: C
options.body: When you need only sub-millisecond key/value lookups

options.label: D
options.body: When you need a relational warehouse with concurrency scaling for BI

explanation: Glue shines for managed/serverless ETL. EMR is better for custom/long-lived cluster control. Key/value and warehouse needs point to other services.

stem: An application must retain stream data for custom consumers with shard-level processing and optional enhanced fan-out. Which service fits best?

options.label: A
options.body: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams

options.label: B
options.body: Amazon Data Firehose alone as the system of record for consumer fan-out

options.label: C
options.body: Amazon Athena

options.label: D
options.body: Amazon S3 Inventory

explanation: Kinesis Data Streams is built for durable streaming with consumer applications. Firehose is primarily a delivery stream to destinations, not a general consumer fan-out system of record.

stem: Telemetry must be ingested continuously and landed into S3 as near-real-time buffered objects with optional format conversion, without managing consumers. Which service is the most direct fit?

options.label: A
options.body: Amazon Data Firehose

options.label: B
options.body: Amazon Redshift Spectrum

options.label: C
options.body: AWS Glue DataBrew

options.label: D
options.body: AWS Certificate Manager

explanation: Firehose is managed delivery into destinations such as S3 with buffering and optional conversion.

stem: A healthcare partner requires digitally signed, encrypted file exchange with integrity checks and receipts for B2B claims files. Which AWS Transfer Family protocol is the best fit?

options.label: A
options.body: AS2

options.label: B
options.body: Anonymous FTP without TLS

options.label: C
options.body: SMTP email drop boxes

options.label: D
options.body: Public S3 website hosting

explanation: AS2 is commonly used for B2B signed/encrypted document exchange with MDNs/receipts. The other options lack that compliance-oriented exchange model.

stem: QuickSight dashboards repeatedly run the same expensive multi-join aggregate against Redshift while underlying data changes only a few times per day. Which Redshift feature best improves dashboard load time?

options.label: A
options.body: Materialized views refreshed on the data change cadence

options.label: B
options.body: Disabling result caching permanently

options.label: C
options.body: Converting all facts to SUPER JSON without modeling

options.label: D
options.body: Moving the cluster to a single-node type only

explanation: Materialized views precompute expensive aggregates for repeated queries when data freshness needs are modest.

stem: A Glue ETL job writes DynamicFrames to S3 with partitionKeys but analysts cannot query new partitions in Athena until a separate crawler runs. How can the job register partitions during the write?

options.label: A
options.body: Enable partition projection or use a sink option / catalog update pattern such as enabling updateBehavior/partition updates so partitions are registered as data is written

options.label: B
options.body: Delete the Glue Data Catalog and rely on listing S3 keys in the Athena UI only

options.label: C
options.body: Store Parquet in Glacier Instant Retrieval only

options.label: D
options.body: Switch from Athena to AWS CloudTrail Lake for table reads

explanation: Glue can update the Data Catalog with new partitions as part of the write path, avoiding a delayed crawler-only workflow.

stem: A Glue crawler will catalog a DynamoDB table. Which configuration detail is specific to DynamoDB versus an S3 data store?

options.label: A
options.body: Sampling configuration / scan rate considerations for reading table items to infer schema

options.label: B
options.body: Choosing an S3 path depth for partition discovery

options.label: C
options.body: Setting an Amazon S3 inventory manifest as the crawler target

options.label: D
options.body: Enabling S3 dual-layer server-side encryption on the crawler itself

explanation: DynamoDB crawlers sample/scan table items and expose scan-rate related settings. S3 path depth and inventory manifests apply to object stores.

stem: An S3 Lifecycle rule transitions objects tagged project=archive after 60 days. Operators remove the tag from objects that must be retained. Which two statements are accurate operationally?

options.label: A
options.body: Lifecycle evaluates object tags; removing the tag can exclude the object from that tag-filtered rule on subsequent evaluations

options.label: B
options.body: Use S3 Inventory or Storage Lens / listings plus rule understanding to verify expected transitions rather than assuming instant UI certainty alone

options.label: C
options.body: Lifecycle rules permanently ignore tag changes after the object is created

options.label: D
options.body: Tag removal always restores objects already in Glacier Instantaneously to Standard without a restore

options.label: E
options.body: Lifecycle only works on buckets without versioning and cannot coexist with tags

explanation: Tag-based lifecycle rules re-evaluate eligibility; removing tags can prevent future transitions. Already transitioned objects are not magically restored by untagging.

stem: A rule intends Standard → Standard-IA at 30 days → Glacier Flexible Retrieval at 45 days. Which statement reflects S3 transition constraints?

options.label: A
options.body: Transition timelines must respect minimum days and supported transition paths between storage classes

options.label: B
options.body: Any storage class can transition to any other class after one day with no restrictions

options.label: C
options.body: Lifecycle transitions require AWS Glue crawlers to rewrite objects

options.label: D
options.body: Objects smaller than 128 KB always transition faster than larger objects by rule

explanation: S3 enforces minimum ages and valid transition graphs between classes. Not every hop is unrestricted.

stem: A 40-row region_lookup dimension is joined to large KEY-distributed facts. Which distribution style keeps the join local on every node without redistributing the dimension?

options.label: A
options.body: ALL distribution for region_lookup

options.label: B
options.body: EVEN for region_lookup and KEY on a low-cardinality column for facts

options.label: C
options.body: AUTO only with no further thought when the table is tiny and joined everywhere

options.label: D
options.body: Disabling compression encodings

explanation: ALL copies small dimensions to every node so joins to large facts avoid redistributing the dimension.

stem: Auditors need to know which training dataset and preprocessing job produced a model on a SageMaker endpoint. Which capability is purpose-built for this traceability?

options.label: A
options.body: Amazon SageMaker ML Lineage Tracking (and related catalog/lineage features)

options.label: B
options.body: Amazon SQS dead-letter queues

options.label: C
options.body: Amazon Route 53 health checks

options.label: D
options.body: AWS Snowball Edge device manifests alone

explanation: SageMaker lineage tracking records relationships among data, jobs, and models.

stem: Analysts need infrequent ad-hoc SQL over CSV/JSON in S3 with minimal ongoing cost and no cluster to manage. Which approach is most cost-effective?

options.label: A
options.body: Catalog with Glue crawler and query via Athena (optionally with workgroup limits)

options.label: B
options.body: Always load into a provisioned Redshift cluster first for every ad-hoc question

options.label: C
options.body: Duplicate all files into Amazon RDS MySQL daily

options.label: D
options.body: Use only QuickSight SPICE with no SQL access

explanation: Athena is serverless SQL on S3 and fits sporadic ad-hoc analysis. Provisioned warehouses add steady cost.

stem: Multiple departments share an S3 data lake and need least-privilege access to different subsets with low operational overhead. Which design fits best?

options.label: A
options.body: AWS Lake Formation with LF-Tags / tag-based access control on Data Catalog resources

options.label: B
options.body: A single shared IAM user access key distributed to every analyst

options.label: C
options.body: Public bucket ACLs for convenience

options.label: D
options.body: Copying the entire lake into per-analyst laptops nightly

explanation: Lake Formation TBAC is purpose-built for fine-grained lake permissions with less policy sprawl than path-only IAM at scale.

stem: Hundreds of customer-specific Glue jobs must start at 2 AM in each customer’s time zone with varying payloads as customers are added. Which approach scales best?

options.label: A
options.body: Manage per-customer EventBridge Scheduler schedules (or equivalent schedule resources) driven by customer config data

options.label: B
options.body: One global cron that ignores time zones

options.label: C
options.body: Manual starts by an on-call engineer for each customer

options.label: D
options.body: Embedding wall-clock sleeps inside Glue Spark drivers for each customer

explanation: EventBridge Scheduler scales to many one-off schedules with timezone support better than manual or single global cron approaches.

stem: A Lambda must run when any Glue job in the account enters FAILED, without polling. Which two elements are part of a sound design?

options.label: A
options.body: Capture Glue job state-change events via EventBridge

options.label: B
options.body: Set the Lambda as the EventBridge rule target filtered to FAILED

options.label: C
options.body: Run a Lambda every second calling GetJobRuns for all jobs

options.label: D
options.body: Disable CloudWatch metrics for Glue to reduce noise

options.label: E
options.body: Require SSH into Glue’s underlying hosts

explanation: EventBridge can route Glue job state changes to Lambda. Polling and host access are unnecessary and fragile.

stem: An engineer needs a one-hour ad-hoc distinct-count query on Parquet in S3 without provisioning clusters. Which service fits best?

options.label: A
options.body: Amazon Athena

options.label: B
options.body: Amazon Redshift provisioned cluster created for one query then deleted mid-hour without automation

options.label: C
options.body: Amazon EC2 with a manual Hadoop install for a single COUNT DISTINCT

options.label: D
options.body: AWS Budgets

explanation: Athena provides serverless SQL on S3 for ad-hoc analysis.

stem: Exploratory Spark analysis is bursty a few hours per week. Which factor most favors Athena Spark notebooks over a long-running EMR cluster?

options.label: A
options.body: Serverless on-demand compute that avoids paying for idle cluster capacity

options.label: B
options.body: Need for persistent HDFS with custom bootstrap AMI deep customization

options.label: C
options.body: Requirement to pin exact EC2 instance families for years

options.label: D
options.body: Need for OS-level SSH into every executor host daily

explanation: Athena Spark notebooks suit intermittent exploration without idle cluster cost.

stem: Terabytes of microservice logs need full-text search, dashboards, and cost-effective long-term retention. Which approach is most appropriate?

options.label: A
options.body: Hot searchable store such as OpenSearch for recent/queryable logs plus durable cheap storage (for example S3) for long-term retention tiers

options.label: B
options.body: Only print logs to application stdout with no aggregation

options.label: C
options.body: Store all logs exclusively in DynamoDB strongly consistent items forever

options.label: D
options.body: Email each log line via SES

explanation: Search engines handle interactive full-text needs; object storage tiers handle cheap long retention.

stem: A CloudWatch Logs Insights query must count errors by service field in 5-minute bins, sort descending, and limit to top 20. Which components belong in the query pipeline?

options.label: A
options.body: stats count() by service, bin(5m)

options.label: B
options.body: sort count desc | limit 20 (or equivalent sort/limit clauses)

options.label: C
options.body: DELETE FROM log group

options.label: D
options.body: VACUUM FULL on the log group

options.label: E
options.body: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY

explanation: Logs Insights uses stats/bin aggregations with sort and limit. Relational DDL/maintenance statements do not apply.

stem: Five numeric DataBrew columns must each be ≤ 100. How can one rule cover all five columns?

options.label: A
options.body: Define a column-level check once and apply it to multiple columns in the ruleset

options.label: B
options.body: Create five separate Glue workflows that each drop the table

options.label: C
options.body: Use Route 53 latency-based routing

options.label: D
options.body: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the DataBrew project

explanation: DataBrew rulesets support applying the same check across multiple columns.

stem: Glue Spark jobs sometimes suffer shuffle skew. The team wants Spark to detect and correct skewed partitions at runtime. Which statements are correct about adaptive execution-style capabilities?

options.label: A
options.body: Adaptive Query Execution can coalesce/optimize skewed shuffle partitions based on runtime stats

options.label: B
options.body: Enabling AQE-related settings can reduce manual salting for many skew cases

options.label: C
options.body: AQE requires disabling the Glue Data Catalog permanently

options.label: D
options.body: Skew is impossible on Parquet inputs

options.label: E
options.body: The only fix is always converting to CSV

explanation: AQE uses runtime statistics to mitigate skew; it does not require abandoning the catalog or changing to CSV.

stem: Training data in S3 needs data quality rules with minimal operational overhead before ML use. Which approach fits best?

options.label: A
options.body: Glue DataBrew profile jobs with rulesets, optionally triggered via EventBridge on new data

options.label: B
options.body: A perpetual EMR cluster running custom code for every object with no managed rules

options.label: C
options.body: Neptune ML Gremlin scripts as the primary DQ engine for tabular training sets

options.label: D
options.body: DynamoDB global tables to deduplicate S3 objects

explanation: DataBrew provides managed profiling and rules with low ops overhead for tabular quality checks.

stem: An S3 Access Point should accept requests only from a specific VPC. Which statements are correct?

options.label: A
options.body: You can restrict an access point policy to a VPC source VPC condition

options.label: B
options.body: Network origin controls on the access point help ensure requests come from the designated VPC

options.label: C
options.body: Access points replace the need for any IAM authorization always

options.label: D
options.body: VPC-only access points automatically make the bucket world-readable

options.label: E
options.body: Access points can only be used with Glacier Deep Archive listings

explanation: Access points support VPC-restricted policies/network origins while IAM still authorizes actions.

stem: Which option is best described as unmanaged relative to a managed database service, where the customer patches OS and database engine?

options.label: A
options.body: Running a database on Amazon EC2

options.label: B
options.body: Amazon RDS

options.label: C
options.body: Amazon Aurora fully managed clusters

options.label: D
options.body: Amazon DynamoDB

explanation: EC2-hosted databases shift OS/engine patching to the customer versus RDS/Aurora/DynamoDB managed models.

stem: An EC2 ETL job hard-codes an RDS password. Security requires removing the hard-coded secret and rotating credentials without redeploying the app each rotation. Which two actions help?

options.label: A
options.body: Store credentials in AWS Secrets Manager

options.label: B
options.body: Enable rotation and have the application retrieve the secret at runtime

options.label: C
options.body: Commit the password to a public GitHub gist for centralized access

options.label: D
options.body: Disable SSL on RDS to simplify clients

options.label: E
options.body: Share one IAM access key in Slack

explanation: Secrets Manager plus runtime retrieval enables rotation without baking passwords into builds.

stem: Engineers should gain access to S3/Glue resources tagged with the same project tag they are assigned, without rewriting policies for each project change. Which two elements implement ABAC?

options.label: A
options.body: Tag principals (users/roles) with a project tag

options.label: B
options.body: Write policies that compare resource tags to principal tags (aws:PrincipalTag / aws:ResourceTag)

options.label: C
options.body: Disable all tagging on resources

options.label: D
options.body: Use only inline wildcard Allow * on * for everyone

options.label: E
options.body: Store passwords in object metadata instead of IAM

explanation: ABAC matches principal tags to resource tags in IAM conditions.

stem: On-premises ETL connects to Redshift over the internet. Auditors require encryption in transit and rejection of unencrypted attempts. What should be configured?

options.label: A
options.body: Require TLS for connections (for example require_ssl / equivalent cluster parameter) so non-TLS clients fail

options.label: B
options.body: Disable encryption to improve speed for auditors

options.label: C
options.body: Use only HTTP cleartext JDBC

options.label: D
options.body: Expose the cluster with a wide-open 0.0.0.0/0 security group and no TLS

explanation: Requiring SSL/TLS on the Redshift cluster rejects unencrypted clients.

stem: A short-lived Glue job must decrypt objects under a customer managed KMS key for one run without permanently widening key or role policies. Which approach fits?

options.label: A
options.body: Use a KMS grant for temporary permission

options.label: B
options.body: Rely on grant constraints/retirement so access is narrowly scoped and temporary

options.label: C
options.body: Make the CMK publicly usable by anonymous principals

options.label: D
options.body: Disable CloudTrail for the account during the job

options.label: E
options.body: Embed the raw KMS key material in the Glue script

explanation: KMS grants provide temporary, retiring permissions without permanent policy edits.

stem: Organization CloudTrail already delivers logs to a centralized S3 bucket. Auditors need one-off SQL for DeleteBucket calls this quarter with minimal new infrastructure. What is the leanest approach?

options.label: A
options.body: Query the existing CloudTrail S3 logs with Athena (and Glue catalog/partitions as needed)

options.label: B
options.body: Rebuild a new streaming pipeline into a dedicated Redshift cluster solely for this quarter’s question

options.label: C
options.body: Turn off CloudTrail and rely on memory of console clicks

options.label: D
options.body: Use Amazon Polly to read log files aloud

explanation: Athena on existing CloudTrail S3 data answers ad-hoc audit SQL with little new infrastructure. AWS Config is better for configuration timeline questions; here the need is API call search.
